global_rating_descriptors.fail: Disorganised or unsafe. Misses most key information or red flags; communication damages rapport.
global_rating_descriptors.borderline: Gathers some key information but with important omissions; reasoning is weak or poorly justified.
global_rating_descriptors.pass: Safe, reasonably structured history covering the key features; sensible differential and plan.
global_rating_descriptors.good: Fluent, patient-centred history; elicits red flags; well-justified differentials and appropriate plan.
global_rating_descriptors.excellent: Polished and efficient. Patient-centred throughout, comprehensive yet focused, with intern-ready reasoning and safety-netting.

items.label: Introduces self and role; confirms patient identity
Gains consent and opens with an open question
Listens without early interruption and picks up cues
Explores the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations
Acknowledges and responds to emotion with empathy
Uses plain language and avoids jargon
Summarises back to the patient and invites corrections
Explains next steps and closes the consultation
Takes a medication and allergy history
Presents in a clear structure: summary, positives, negatives, differentials, plan
Links findings to differentials and justifies their ranking
Recognises the urgency of the presentation
